title: Acceptance from the emitted verdict
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $y$ be a Boolean word. Suppose $M$ halts within $T$ steps on $y$ and outputs the Boolean indicator of membership in $V$. Then every step before time $T$ emits either no bit or the bit true if and only if $y\in V$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$V$ is a language of Boolean words
$M$ computes the membership indicator of $y$ within $T$ steps
replaced: Let a machine compute, on input $y$ within time $T$, the single indicator bit of membership of $y$ in a language $V$. Then no snapshot before time $T$ emits the bit false exactly when $y \in V$; silent or junk traces cannot satisfy this equivalence, because the total decider supplies its actual verdict bit.
